strategy.summary: TestForge's axe scan found / and /contact free of violations with no axe check guarding them. Add an axe check (via the repo's existing @axe-core/playwright devDependency) as a new test in the e2e spec that already opens each page, failing on any violation of impact minor or worse and naming each rule and its elements. No new violations were reported, so no defects are recorded; the known color-contrast on /about and image-alt on /cart are left alone.
inScope: A shared helper tests/helpers/axe.js that runs axe and returns the violations at minor-or-worse impact, used by both specs
outOfScope: Known violations color-contrast on /about and image-alt on /cart (earlier runs' issues are open)
Keyboard and screen-reader behaviour, which axe cannot prove
assumptions: The real app (node server.js, started by playwright.config.js webServer on port 4174) runs for real; nothing is faked.
Each axe check is a new test added to the existing spec file that opens the page; existing tests and their assertions stay unchanged.
Impacts guarded: minor, moderate, serious, critical (the work item reports minor or worse), stricter than the skill's critical/serious default because both pages pass at every impact today.

candidates.text: TestForge's axe_checks gate only counts a page as guarded when the spec file that does page.goto('<path>') itself calls `new AxeBuilder({ page }).analyze()`; hiding the AxeBuilder call in a helper fails the gate. Keep analyze() in the spec and share only the impact filter (tests/helpers/axe.js guardedViolations(results)).
candidates.evidence: self_check reported '/ passed the scan but no changed e2e test checks it with axe' until AxeBuilder moved from tests/helpers/axe.js into tests/home.spec.js and tests/contact.spec.js
